title: Audit: emit events for Dedicated capacity scaling (before/after + initiator)
author: Nadia Rahman
description: Motivation: Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin changes are considered sensitive actions (availability + billing impact). We had partial logging in the control plane, but scaling via autoscaler and a few console/admin code paths did not emit schema-v1 audit events reliably (see SUP-4977). This PR instruments the Dedicated capacity controller + autoscaler with canonical audit events, including before/after capacity values and a normalized initiator field (manual vs auto). Scope: (1) Emit audit events for scale request + applied scale for dedicated pools, (2) include before/after desired_capacity and min/max bounds, (3) attribute actor correctly for console/admin vs service-initiated changes, and (4) add tests + registry entries to keep naming/schema validation enforced. Event names (schema v1): dedicated.capacity.scale_requested, dedicated.capacity.scale_applied, dedicated.capacity.quota_updated. Payload notes: includes capacity_pool_id, dedicated_cluster_id (when available), region, prev_desired_capacity, new_desired_capacity, prev_min/max, new_min/max, initiator={manual|auto}, and change_reason (e.g. "autoscaler/queue_depth" or "admin/console"). Actor attribution: manual actions use end-user actor from gateway (user_id, email when available); auto actions use service principal (service.name=dedicated-autoscaler) with on_behalf_of omitted. Outcome semantics: we emit scale_requested even if scale_application fails; scale_applied includes outcome=success|failure and error.code/error.message (sanitized) when failures occur. Correlation: request_id is propagated through control-plane handlers; autoscaler emits a synthetic request_id and sets trace_id if present. Backward compat: no dual-write here (Dedicated had no stable legacy audit event names); this is additive. Rollout: guarded by AUDIT_DEDICATED_SCALING_EVENTS=1 env flag (default on in staging, off in prod until after exporter backlog work completes).
commits: audit(dedicated): emit schema-v1 events for scale request/apply
audit(dedicated): add initiator normalization (manual vs auto) + reason codes
control-plane: propagate request_id to dedicated controller actions
audit(registry): register dedicated.* event names + examples
tests: add dedicated scaling audit event unit tests + redaction assertions
docs: update internal dev notes for dedicated scaling events
conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Can we confirm these are included in the sensitive actions inventory and that payloads do not leak internal IDs that customers shouldn't see? Also please ensure error.message is sanitized (no stack traces).

Nadia Rahman (Author): Yes — mapped under ENG-2486 (Dedicated scaling/quota). Payload uses customer-visible capacity_pool_id + region; dedicated_cluster_id is included only when the cluster is customer-owned (Dedicated) and already visible in Console. Error messages go through auditSanitizeError() (drops stack, trims message, whitelists code). Added a regression test asserting no 'stack' field and no raw exception serialization.
Rafael Mendes (SRE): A bit worried about event volume from autoscaler loops. How often do we emit scale_requested? Per evaluation tick or only on changes?

Nadia Rahman (Author): Only on actual desired_capacity change (prev != next). Also added a 60s coalesce window per pool for repeated oscillations to avoid spamming on flaps; scale_applied emits only when we actually reconcile and update the pool.
Allison Grant (Observability): Please align metric names / tags with audit pipeline standards. Also, request_id for autoscaler should be deterministic-ish for correlation (otherwise hard to debug).

Nadia Rahman (Author): Metrics are unchanged in this PR (audit events only), but tags match the audit schema fields (org_id, region, capacity_pool_id). For autoscaler request_id we generate a UUIDv7 and set actor.type=service; we also attach trace_id if the autoscaler loop is traced. Added 'initiator=auto' and 'change_reason' for troubleshooting.
Diego Santos (Cross-deploy): For Dedicated + Private parity, can we keep initiator and reason fields consistent with Private installer events?
Nadia Rahman (Author): Yep — using libs/audit-logging/src/initiator.ts helper shared by Private installer work. Fields: initiator, initiator_detail (optional), change_reason (string).
Mei Lin (Reporting): Please ensure the coverage scanner can detect these event names. Are they registered in the audit-event registry JSON?
Nadia Rahman (Author): Added registry/events/dedicated.json entries + examples; build-time registry check now passes and coverage scanner picks them up under the Dedicated subsystem.
release_notes: Dedicated: scaling and quota/admin actions now emit schema-v1 audit events with before/after capacity values and initiator (manual vs auto).
Improved actor attribution for autoscaler-initiated scaling changes (service principal) vs console/admin actions (end-user).
